facts.statement: Misrepresenting policy terms or benefits, or misrepresenting to induce a policyholder to lapse, forfeit or surrender, is an unfair practice.
facts.quote: making any misrepresentation to any policyholder insured in any company for the purpose of inducing or tending to induce such policyholder to lapse, forfeit, or surrender his insurance

items.stem: A producer tells a policyholder that her whole life policy's cash value will be forfeited next year unless she surrenders it now. The statement is false, and the producer is not offering her another policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 prohibits misrepresentations made to a policyholder to induce a lapse, forfeiture or surrender. Lying about the policy's terms to get her to surrender is misrepresentation.

facts.statement: Advertising or statements about the business of insurance that are untrue, deceptive or misleading are prohibited.
facts.quote: an advertisement, announcement or statement containing any assertion, representation or statement with respect to the business of insurance or with respect to any person in the conduct of his insurance business, which is untrue, deceptive or misleading

items.stem: An agency's website and brochures tell the public it "won the state's top customer service award five years running." No such award exists. Which unfair trade practice is this?
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 prohibits any advertisement or statement about the business of insurance that is untrue, deceptive or misleading, in any medium including radio.

facts.statement: Defamation is a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurer's financial condition calculated to injure someone in the insurance business.
facts.quote: which is false, or maliciously critical of or derogatory to the financial condition of an insurer, and which is calculated to injure any person engaged in the business of insurance

items.stem: A producer tells prospects that a competing insurer "is about to be taken over by regulators," which is untrue, to steer new business away from that insurer. Which practice is this?
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 defines defamation as a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurer's financial condition that is calculated to injure a person in the insurance business.

facts.statement: Boycott, coercion or intimidation that restrains or monopolizes the business of insurance is an unfair practice.
facts.quote: any act of boycott, coercion or intimidation resulting in or tending to result in unreasonable restraint of, or monopoly in, the business of insurance

items.stem: Several insurers agree among themselves to stop writing business through any agency that also places business with a new competitor, so the competitor cannot get established. This is an example of:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 prohibits concerted acts of boycott, coercion or intimidation that unreasonably restrain, or create a monopoly in, the business of insurance.

facts.statement: Unfair discrimination in life insurance rates between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life is prohibited.
facts.quote: any unfair discrimination between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life in the rates charged for any contract of life insurance

items.stem: Two applicants have the same age, health and risk class, with equal life expectancy. The underwriter charges one of them a higher life insurance rate because of the neighborhood he lives in. Under New Jersey law, this is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 prohibits unfair discrimination in life insurance rates between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life.

facts.statement: Discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry in issuing, withholding, extending or renewing any policy is prohibited.
facts.quote: because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry of such person or group of persons in the issuance, withholding, extension or renewal of any policy of insurance

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics listed in New Jersey's ban on discrimination in issuing, withholding, extending or renewing a policy?
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 bans discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry. Occupation is a legitimate underwriting factor and is not on the list.

facts.statement: Giving a rebate of premium, or any valuable consideration not specified in the contract, as an inducement to buy life, annuity or health insurance is a prohibited rebate.
facts.quote: any rebate of premiums payable on the contract, or any special favor or advantage in the dividends or other benefits thereon, or any valuable consideration or inducement whatsoever not specified in the contract

items.stem: To close a life insurance sale, a producer offers to pay the client's first month's premium out of his own pocket. This is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 prohibits paying any rebate of premium or other valuable consideration not specified in the contract as an inducement to buy insurance. Paying the client's premium is a rebate.

facts.statement: Fair and equitable bonuses or premium abatements paid to policyholders out of surplus from nonparticipating insurance are not rebates or unfair discrimination.
facts.quote: paying bonuses to policyholders or otherwise abating their premiums in whole or in part out of surplus accumulated from nonparticipating insurance; provided, that any such bonuses or abatement of premiums shall be fair and equitable to policyholders

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT treated as a rebate or unfair discrimination under New Jersey law?
options: Fair bonuses paid out of nonparticipating surplus
Fair bonuses out of surplus for policyholders who buy more
Premium reductions promised verbally but not in the contract
Insurer stock given to every new policyholder
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 excludes from rebating and discrimination the payment of fair and equitable bonuses or premium abatements to life policyholders out of surplus from nonparticipating insurance.

facts.statement: Readjusting a group policy's premium rate on loss or expense experience at the end of a policy year is permitted, retroactive only for that policy year.
facts.quote: readjustment of the rate of premium for a group policy based on the loss or expense experience thereunder, at the end of the first or any subsequent policy year of insurance thereunder, which may be made retroactive only for such policy year

items.stem: At the end of a policy year, a group life insurer readjusts the group's premium rate based on the group's loss experience. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: An illegal rebate to the group
Permitted, retroactive only for that policy year
Permitted, retroactive for up to three prior years
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 treats a group premium readjustment based on loss or expense experience as neither a rebate nor discrimination, and allows it to be retroactive only for that policy year.

facts.statement: Improper claim handling is an unfair claim settlement practice when committed with such frequency as to indicate a general business practice.
facts.quote: Committing or performing with such frequency as to indicate a general business practice any of the following

items.stem: Under New Jersey's unfair trade practices law, improper claim handling by an insurer is an unfair claim settlement practice when it is committed:
options: Even once, against any single claimant
With enough frequency to affect ten or more claimants
Only in ways the commissioner has published in advance
Often enough to indicate a general business practice
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 defines unfair claim settlement practices as listed acts committed with such frequency as to indicate a general business practice.

facts.statement: Refusing to pay claims without a reasonable investigation based on all available information is an unfair claim settlement practice.
facts.quote: (d) Refusing to pay claims without conducting a reasonable investigation based upon all available information;

items.stem: An insurer's claim unit routinely denies life claims that show any red flag, without first gathering the information available to it. Which New Jersey rule does this practice violate?
options: The 45-day written notice rule for delayed claims
The unfair claim settlement practices rule
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 lists refusing to pay claims without conducting a reasonable investigation based on all available information as an unfair claim settlement practice. Requesting proof of death and investigating contestable claims are normal practice.
items.retired: Failed the test-wise check in three review rounds; the conduct is identifiable by common sense. V4-10a and V4-12a cover the claim settlement rule.

facts.statement: Paying claims without a statement of the coverage under which payment is made is an unfair claim settlement practice.
facts.quote: (j) Making claims payments to insureds or beneficiaries not accompanied by a statement setting forth the coverage under which the payments are being made;

items.stem: An insurer routinely sends claim payments to beneficiaries without saying which coverage each payment falls under. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Acceptable if the amount paid is correct
A violation only for health insurance claims
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 lists making claim payments without a statement of the coverage under which they are made as an unfair claim settlement practice.

facts.statement: An insurer must keep a complete record of all complaints received since its last examination.
facts.quote: Failure of any person to maintain a complete record of all the complaints which it has received since the date of its last examination.

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, an insurer must keep a complete record of all complaints it has received since:
options: The start of the current calendar year
The date it was first licensed
The date five years before the current one
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 requires a complete record of all complaints received since the date of the last examination, including their number, line, nature, disposition and processing time.

facts.statement: For the complaint record, a complaint is any written communication primarily expressing a grievance.
facts.quote: “complaint” shall mean any written communication primarily expressing a grievance

items.stem: For New Jersey's complaint record requirement, a "complaint" is defined as:
options: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction
Any grievance filed with the Department of Banking and Insurance
Any written request for policy information
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 defines a complaint, for the record-keeping requirement, as any written communication primarily expressing a grievance.

facts.statement: An insurer's complaint record must show the total number of complaints, their classification by line, the nature and disposition of each, and the time taken to process each.
facts.quote: This record shall indicate the total number of complaints, their classification by line of insurance, the nature of each complaint, the disposition of these complaints, and the time it took to process each complaint.

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, an insurer's complaint record must show each of the following EXCEPT:
options: The processing time for each complaint
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17:29B-4 requires the complaint record to show the total number of complaints, their classification by line of insurance, and the nature, disposition and processing time of each. The selling producer is not a required element.

facts.statement: Lower rates for policies on payroll deduction, bank draft or similar plans are not unfair discrimination if reasonably related to the savings from the plan.
facts.quote: such rate or underwriting considerations being reasonably related to the savings made by the use of such plan

items.stem: An insurer charges a slightly lower premium to policyholders who pay by monthly payroll deduction. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Allowed, if the lower rate reflects the savings from the plan
Unfair discrimination between policyholders of the same class
Allowed, if the agent's commission is reduced by the same amount
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-14 allows lower rates on payroll deduction and similar plans when the rate is reasonably related to the savings made by using the plan.

facts.statement: The ban on rebates and inducements applies whether or not a policy is ultimately issued.
facts.quote: The provisions of this section shall apply whether or not a contract of insurance is ultimately effected.

items.stem: A producer offers a prospect a $200 gift card if she buys a life policy. She declines and never applies. Under New Jersey rules:
options: A violation, since the offer alone breaks the rule
No violation, since no policy was sold
A violation, but just if she had applied
No violation, if the gift card is worth under $25
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:17A-2.3(a)-(e) bars offering an inducement not plainly expressed in the contract, and applies whether or not a contract of insurance is ultimately effected.

facts.statement: A producer may not give anything of value in return for a person's agreement not to buy insurance from another producer or insurer.
facts.quote: anything of value in return for that person's agreement not to purchase insurance from another insurance producer or insurer

items.stem: A producer offers a business owner free tax preparation for a year in exchange for a promise not to buy insurance from any competing agency. Under New Jersey rules, this is:
options: Prohibited, as value for not buying elsewhere
Allowed, since tax preparation is not insurance
Allowed, if the services are worth under $100
Prohibited, once she actually buys a policy
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:17A-2.3(a)-(e) bars giving anything of value in return for a person's agreement not to purchase insurance from another producer or insurer, whether or not a policy is sold.
items.retired: Answerable by ethics instinct alone after a rewrite.

facts.statement: Twisting is a misleading representation or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of policies or insurers to induce someone to lapse, surrender or replace a policy.
facts.quote: make any misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of any insurance policies or annuity contracts or insurers

items.stem: A producer shows a client a comparison that leaves out her existing whole life policy's cash value, to persuade her to surrender it and buy a new policy from another insurer. This practice is called:
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:17A-2.8, titled "Twisting" prohibited, bars misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparisons of policies or insurers made to induce a person to lapse, surrender or replace a policy.
